name: W loop rule
summary: Between a W split and a W merge, a wire with Z(π) cancels a plain wire.
description:
The W-spider (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg.

Splitting with a W-spider and merging again with $k$ parallel wires gives $\mathrm{diag}(1, k)$: the excitation can take any of the $k$ routes. A wire carrying a Pauli Z contributes $-1$ instead of $+1$, so $n$ plain wires and $m \leq n$ wires with Z can be replaced by $n - m$ plain wires. This is Hadzihasanovic's generalised loop rule $\mathrm{lp}_W^{n,m}$, a form of integer arithmetic inside the ZW-calculus; the case $n = m = 1$ is the [W Hopf rule](../w-hopf/). The stored instance has $n = 2$ and $m = 1$.

With arbitrary labels on the wires it becomes the [sum rule](../w-sum/).
parameter_notes: $n$ plain wires and $m$ wires with Z(π) on the left, $n-m$ plain wires on the right; holds for all $n \geq m$.

source.location: Section 3 (The rules), generalised loop rule I, $\mathrm{lp}_W^{n,m}$
